SUPABIZ FACTORY MAP — 18 OCTOBER 2026

metadata: 
  title: SupaBiz factory map
  version: 1.0
  date: 2026-10-18
  status: Proposed work breakdown; not implemented product inventory
  basis: Existing 18 saved reviews and v4 synthesis. No new vendor runtime audit.
  interpretation: A common lifecycle for SupaBiz. Specialist companies cover subsets, not necessarily all stations. Comparisons are documented differentiators or design interpretations; unknown vendor signup/auth internals remain unknown.
  counting: 12 stations × 5 responsibility packages = 60; 4 shared foundations × 4 packages = 16; total 76 planning packages. These are not 76 services, screens, repositories or equal-size tasks. Each package has one ID; station delivery consumes shared foundations without recounting them.
  sequence: 01–04 establish and maintain setup; 05–11 repeat for work; 12 improves reviewed behavior. Dependencies overlap; security/evaluation start before live execution. Not every event calls a model, needs human approval or changes a learned rule.
stations: 
  - id: 01
    name: Join & establish trust
    phase: SET UP
    question: Who owns this workspace?
    purpose: Create a customer and business boundary before granting access. Signup is required for SupaBiz; the saved reviews do not establish every vendor’s signup implementation.
    parts: 
      - id: 01.1
        name: Account & sign-in
        deliverable: Maintained identity provider, sessions and recovery.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 01.2
        name: Business workspace
        deliverable: Organization, outlets or chambers, and verified ownership.
        mode: Build
      - id: 01.3
        name: People & roles
        deliverable: Invitations, membership, manager/staff/CA roles and removal.
        mode: Build
      - id: 01.4
        name: Consent & boundaries
        deliverable: Explain selected access, purposes, retention and who sees what.
        mode: Build
      - id: 01.5
        name: Device enrollment
        deliverable: Register a phone/browser; bind optional desktop sessions to a principal.
        mode: Adapt
    inputs: Owner intent and verified identity.
    outputs: Workspace ID, memberships and initial access policy.
    gate: A user in Consu cannot read ForeFathers by switching an ID; removed members lose access.
    loop: Membership changes return here; account deletion has its own retention/export process.
    layers: 
      - L01
      - L02
    sprint: S1
    examples: 
      varun: Varun creates separate Consu and ForeFathers business scopes; staff and CA receive different roles.
      ramya: Arkaj creates the chamber workspace; Ramya can coordinate matters without unrestricted access for every staff member.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox contributes stable agent identity and conversation-bound authority; that is narrower than a complete business signup system.
      - project: YC01
        approach: Executor separates account connections from agent use; study that boundary after identity is established.
      - project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 contributes a recognizable personal agent workspace and continuity across devices; hosted tenancy is not audited.
      - project: YC10
        approach: Glen makes shared context ownership relevant; SupaBiz must own membership and source access rules.
  - id: 02
    name: Connect permitted sources
    phase: SET UP
    question: What may the system access?
    purpose: Connect only the accounts and groups needed for a workflow. Reading, sending, exporting and acting are separate capabilities.
    parts: 
      - id: 02.1
        name: Connection broker
        deliverable: OAuth/session credentials stored outside model context.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 02.2
        name: Source enrollment
        deliverable: Choose Gmail inboxes, WhatsApp groups and permitted app scopes.
        mode: Build
      - id: 02.3
        name: Capability map
        deliverable: Describe actual read/write/media/history limits per adapter.
        mode: Build
      - id: 02.4
        name: Connection health
        deliverable: Expiry, missing scopes, reconnect and coverage indicators.
        mode: Build
      - id: 02.5
        name: Revocation path
        deliverable: Disconnect credentials, stop jobs and invalidate affected context.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Workspace identity, user consent and provider credentials.
    outputs: Scoped connection IDs and a verified capability/coverage record.
    gate: Reconnect safely; never treat a quiet disconnected source as up-to-date. Existing WhatsApp group access remains an adapter validation task.
    loop: Expired access returns here; queued actions recheck permission before dispatch.
    layers: 
      - L02
      - L03
    sprint: S1
    examples: 
      varun: Enroll Consu’s operations group and a separate accountant group. Give the pilot read access before enabling reviewed sends.
      ramya: Connect Arkaj’s court inbox; scope which attachments and matter records staff may receive.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC01
        approach: Executor centralizes integrations and credentials so multiple agents can use authorized connections.
      - project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox distinguishes quiet conversation intake, selective activation and the audience of each conversation.
      - project: YC03
        approach: screenpipe adds local screen/audio awareness, with capture controls; this is a later optional source, not a required connector.
      - project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 demonstrates environment continuity and browser handoff; that does not establish durable WhatsApp intake.
      - project: YC18
        approach: Definite’s read-oriented connection pattern is useful before allowing consequential writes.
  - id: 03
    name: Understand the business
    phase: SET UP
    question: What do these names and messages mean?
    purpose: Build an explicit, owner-reviewed business map. Context must be inspectable and corrected; it is not a hidden personality profile. Initial sync already uses stations 05–07 while this business map is being built.
    parts: 
      - id: 03.1
        name: Entity directory
        deliverable: People, outlets, suppliers, assets, clients and matters with stable IDs.
        mode: Build
      - id: 03.2
        name: Vocabulary & aliases
        deliverable: Map Hinglish names, supplier abbreviations, SKUs and matter-number variants.
        mode: Build
      - id: 03.3
        name: Audience map
        deliverable: Define which group, role or matter can see each kind of evidence.
        mode: Build
      - id: 03.4
        name: Source authority
        deliverable: Assign authoritative sources per field and preserve disagreements.
        mode: Build
      - id: 03.5
        name: Baseline review
        deliverable: Approve opening stock, active matters and known operating constraints.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Permitted history, owner answers, source documents and existing business lists.
    outputs: Versioned business map with explicit unknowns and source provenance.
    gate: Ambiguous “the kitchen” or a repeated matter number produces clarification, not a confident wrong match.
    loop: Corrections and new entities update this map through review; revoked evidence cannot remain universal context.
    layers: 
      - L01
      - L05
      - L02
    sprint: S1–S2
    examples: 
      varun: Learn which kitchen, refrigerator, supplier and unit belong to Consu. Confirm opening stock rather than inferring it from chat.
      ramya: Map court, jurisdiction, case number, parties and staff responsibility; the same number in different courts is not one matter.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC04
        approach: Asakana demonstrates domain mapping from messy orders into structured business entries; backend training methods remain unknown.
      - project: YC08
        approach: Marble contributes supplier/item/unit and inventory semantics, with ordering and receiving treated separately.
      - project: YC05
        approach: Praxis organizes work around matters, documents and responsible people.
      - project: YC10
        approach: Glen contributes scoped retrieval, memory ownership and provenance, not a universal business ledger.
      - project: YC18
        approach: Definite stresses aligning meaning before comparing records; exact checks need comparable quantities and periods.
      - project: YC15
        approach: Shire adds physical locations and floor context for observation-driven work; defer camera-specific mapping.
  - id: 04
    name: Define success & rules
    phase: SET UP
    question: What counts as correctly completed?
    purpose: Configure one workflow pack with valid states, responsibilities, approval thresholds and measurable outcomes before letting agents act.
    parts: 
      - id: 04.1
        name: Workflow pack
        deliverable: Typed states, commands, responsibilities and allowed transitions.
        mode: Build
      - id: 04.2
        name: Approval policy
        deliverable: Define allow, deny, hold and human-review rules by action and scope.
        mode: Build
      - id: 04.3
        name: SOP & knowledge versions
        deliverable: Keep draft, tested and active guidance separate.
        mode: Build
      - id: 04.4
        name: Reference scenarios
        deliverable: Protected expected outcomes, forbidden effects and representative ambiguity.
        mode: Build
      - id: 04.5
        name: Activation & cutover
        deliverable: Owner-approved pilot scope, read-only shadowing and rollback plan.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Reviewed business map, owner objectives and risk boundaries.
    outputs: Versioned workflow/policy pack plus a pilot acceptance suite.
    gate: A bad workflow or overly permissive rule must fail tests before it becomes active.
    loop: Station 12 proposes changes here; no silent self-modification.
    layers: 
      - L07
      - L10
      - L06
    sprint: S0–S2
    examples: 
      varun: Define who can assign a maintenance issue, what proof closes it, and when a purchase needs Varun’s approval.
      ramya: Define matter routing, reviewed hearing/deadline types and who may approve changes or share documents.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC12
        approach: GrepAI turns repeated work into procedures, with a useful distinction between drafts and tested active behavior.
      - project: YC06
        approach: Hue contributes repeatable cases and outcome-based release comparisons.
      - project: YC17
        approach: Rystic contributes stateful practice worlds, fault injection and deliberately broken controls.
      - project: YC11
        approach: Decawork contributes action review in business context; hard grants still belong outside a review model.
      - project: YC04
        approach: Asakana inspires corrections that improve later handling, but SupaBiz must design and test the learning mechanism.
  - id: 05
    name: Receive & remember events
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: Did we capture this exactly once?
    purpose: Record permitted source events durably before acknowledging them. Decide whether an event needs work without calling an LLM for every message.
    parts: 
      - id: 05.1
        name: Durable inbox
        deliverable: Persist source identity, timestamps and raw event envelope.
        mode: Build
      - id: 05.2
        name: Sync & backfill
        deliverable: Cursors, reconnect, initial sync and coverage gaps.
        mode: Adapt
      - id: 05.3
        name: Deduplication & revisions
        deliverable: Native IDs, edits, deletes, order and replay rules.
        mode: Build
      - id: 05.4
        name: Wake router
        deliverable: Mentions, event rules and bounded bursts select eligible work.
        mode: Build
      - id: 05.5
        name: Media fetch & quarantine
        deliverable: Fetch references safely; isolate untrusted or unknown sources.
        mode: Build
    inputs: A new message, email, attachment, upload or approved device observation.
    outputs: Durable event ID and queued processing job, or a recorded no-action decision.
    gate: Duplicate, delayed, edited and replayed messages must not create duplicate work or hidden gaps.
    loop: Disconnections route to station 02; recoverable failures retry from the journal.
    layers: 
      - L03
      - L09
    sprint: S1
    examples: 
      varun: A staff member sends “freezer leaking again” with a photo and a follow-up voice note. Capture the burst as evidence before deciding.
      ramya: A court email arrives twice and is later corrected. Preserve both source identity and revision history.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox’s quiet capture and selective wake-up are strong fits for busy WhatsApp groups.
      - project: YC04
        approach: Asakana accepts messy operational messages and attachments as business input.
      - project: YC07
        approach: Sidekick keeps frontline capture in familiar voice/photo/message interactions.
      - project: YC03
        approach: screenpipe is a different intake modality: selected computer activity rather than a business messaging connector.
      - project: YC15
        approach: Shire begins with camera observations; the same intake principles apply, but camera support is optional.
  - id: 06
    name: Read, hear & see evidence
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: What does the source actually say?
    purpose: Extract observations from text, documents, voice, photos and sampled video. Keep source evidence, coverage and uncertainty visible.
    parts: 
      - id: 06.1
        name: Evidence storage
        deliverable: Original media and derived files with independent retention.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 06.2
        name: Document/OCR pipeline
        deliverable: Isolated parsing, page regions and extraction provenance.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 06.3
        name: Speech & language
        deliverable: Transcription with language, translation and timestamp separation.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 06.4
        name: Vision/video adapter
        deliverable: Scoped image analysis or video sampling with coverage limits.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 06.5
        name: Evidence locators
        deliverable: Citations, confidence limitations and useful abstention.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Durable event and authorized original media.
    outputs: Observations linked to page, crop, timestamp or message evidence.
    gate: Noise, missing pages or an unclear quantity yields a useful question; sampled video never becomes proof of unseen events.
    loop: Missing evidence returns to intake or asks the authorized person for clarification.
    layers: 
      - L04
    sprint: S1–S2
    examples: 
      varun: Transcribe Hinglish kitchen audio and identify the visible leak. Do not infer internal freezer temperature from a photograph.
      ramya: Extract the notice’s matter identifier and date with page citations; distinguish publication date from hearing date.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC07
        approach: Sidekick combines frontline voice and visual reports with operational context.
      - project: YC03
        approach: screenpipe illustrates an accessibility/text-before-OCR capture ladder and evidence-linked history.
      - project: YC15
        approach: Shire turns visible camera observations into operational signals; hidden conditions remain unknown.
      - project: YC04
        approach: Asakana turns messages and document/photos into structured candidates for review.
      - project: YC05
        approach: Praxis emphasizes documents as part of a matter’s readiness and work context.
  - id: 07
    name: Form & check business records
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: Which facts can enter the system?
    purpose: Separate observations from candidate records and accepted facts. Exact business checks run before admission; uncertainty is a valid result.
    parts: 
      - id: 07.1
        name: Typed records
        deliverable: Issues, stock movements, invoices, matters and tasks with schemas.
        mode: Build
      - id: 07.2
        name: Entity resolution
        deliverable: Match IDs, aliases and context without merging ambiguous entities.
        mode: Build
      - id: 07.3
        name: Deterministic checks
        deliverable: Exact units, quantities, duplicate references and rule versions.
        mode: Build
      - id: 07.4
        name: Record admission
        deliverable: Version-checked transaction, revision history and outbox.
        mode: Build
      - id: 07.5
        name: Scoped retrieval views
        deliverable: Search/memory projections with provenance and invalidation.
        mode: Adapt
    inputs: Observations, business map, existing records and applicable rules.
    outputs: Accepted revision, rejected candidate or an unresolved check requiring evidence.
    gate: Unknown is not pass; an approval cannot rewrite a false quantity or erase contrary evidence.
    loop: Clarification returns to stations 03/06; new evidence can revise an accepted record while preserving history.
    layers: 
      - L05
      - L02
    sprint: S2
    examples: 
      varun: Create one freezer issue linked to Consu and the asset. In receiving, only accepted quantities create stock movements.
      ramya: Match the email to the correct court and matter, or hold it for Ramya; retain both original and corrected notice.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC18
        approach: Definite contributes a shared record model, exact checks and explicit unresolved outcomes.
      - project: YC08
        approach: Marble distinguishes order, receipt, invoice, credit and settlement; one generic record cannot replace them.
      - project: YC14
        approach: Terse contributes stable entity ownership and guarded mutations; use SQL as the baseline rather than adding a second authority.
      - project: YC10
        approach: Glen contributes permission-aware retrieval and memory lineage; retrieval stays derived from authoritative records.
      - project: YC04
        approach: Asakana makes a structured draft and targeted correction the bridge from messages to business records.
  - id: 08
    name: Plan & assign the work
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: Who does what, by when?
    purpose: The agent proposes bounded next steps. A durable workflow owns assignment, waiting and progression across devices and model calls.
    parts: 
      - id: 08.1
        name: Bounded agent loop
        deliverable: Context selection, tool schemas, budgets and checkpoints.
        mode: Adapt
      - id: 08.2
        name: Durable workflow owner
        deliverable: Persist states, timers and recoverable steps.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 08.3
        name: Assignment & acknowledgement
        deliverable: Responsible person, acceptance and reassignments.
        mode: Build
      - id: 08.4
        name: Deadline & escalation
        deliverable: Durable reminders, blockers and escalation recipients.
        mode: Build
      - id: 08.5
        name: Role-specific work views
        deliverable: Staff task list, manager attention queue and owner summary.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Accepted record, current grants, workflow state and SOP version.
    outputs: Proposed assignment or action with explicit intent, dependencies and owner. Internal state changes also enforce current permissions.
    gate: Sending an assignment is not acceptance; reminders survive worker restarts without duplicate tasks.
    loop: Blocked work asks for evidence or reassignment; long waits do not keep a model process running.
    layers: 
      - L06
      - L07
      - L01
    sprint: S2
    examples: 
      varun: The manager gets a short issue card and assigns a responsible person; missing location prompts one focused question.
      ramya: Ramya reviews the matter and assigns the right staff member with the notice, date type and expected work product.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC05
        approach: Praxis contributes matter-centered coordination, document readiness and clear responsibility.
      - project: YC07
        approach: Sidekick turns frontline reports into operational work with location and follow-up.
      - project: YC13
        approach: herdr’s attention inbox and durable job identity inspire a manager view, though its implementation serves engineering agents.
      - project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 contributes continuity across devices and visible outputs.
      - project: YC12
        approach: GrepAI contributes reusable guarded procedures for repeatable work.
      - project: YC14
        approach: Terse’s short guarded commands and committed views are useful without keeping slow model work inside mutations.
  - id: 09
    name: Authorize the exact action
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: May this action happen now?
    purpose: Every consequential action crosses a policy gate. Low-risk permitted actions may pass automatically; review is conditional, not a mandatory click for every event.
    parts: 
      - id: 09.1
        name: Current permission check
        deliverable: Principal, resource, audience and destination checked at dispatch.
        mode: Build
      - id: 09.2
        name: Intent & approval digest
        deliverable: Bind decision to exact action, record revision and policy version.
        mode: Build
      - id: 09.3
        name: Decision inbox
        deliverable: Allow/deny/hold/needs-context with evidence and changed fields.
        mode: Build
      - id: 09.4
        name: Budget & limit reservation
        deliverable: Reserve allowed spend/quotas before concurrent execution.
        mode: Build
      - id: 09.5
        name: Expiry & revocation
        deliverable: Expire stale approval and re-review changed inputs.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Exact proposed action, current record versions, grants and limits.
    outputs: Authorized intent or denied/held proposal with a reason.
    gate: A changed destination, amount, audience or revoked role invalidates the old approval.
    loop: Held actions return to context/review; no model may override a hard deny.
    layers: 
      - L02
      - L08
      - L01
    sprint: S2
    examples: 
      varun: An internal task may be allowed automatically. A supplier order needs the correct business, amount and approver.
      ramya: Sharing a notice must use the right matter audience; a revised hearing date is reviewed before changing downstream calendars.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC11
        approach: Decawork puts action review outside the acting agent and recognizes missing-context/hold outcomes.
      - project: YC01
        approach: Executor provides approval/credential boundaries to study; the saved review records an approval-consumption race requiring a spike.
      - project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox contributes audience binding and approval tied to the actual proposal.
      - project: YC18
        approach: Definite separates factual checks from approval decisions; approval does not make inconsistent evidence true.
      - project: YC14
        approach: Terse contributes current-version guarded commands; stale state must not authorize an effect.
  - id: 10
    name: Execute through scoped tools
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: Can we do it safely and recover?
    purpose: Execute authorized intent through typed adapters. Use a scoped browser only when a supported API is insufficient and the workflow permits it.
    parts: 
      - id: 10.1
        name: Tool gateway
        deliverable: Typed input/output, adapter version and scoped credential injection.
        mode: Adapt
      - id: 10.2
        name: Effect ledger
        deliverable: Idempotency key, attempt identity and before/after state.
        mode: Build
      - id: 10.3
        name: API & browser execution
        deliverable: Restricted worker, egress, destinations and browser handoff.
        mode: Reuse
      - id: 10.4
        name: Retry & cancellation
        deliverable: Classify pre/post-commit errors; stop the exact worker.
        mode: Build
      - id: 10.5
        name: Delivery & delegation
        deliverable: Audience-safe notifications; job-scoped agent handoff later.
        mode: Adapt
    inputs: Authorized intent with an idempotency key and short-lived execution scope.
    outputs: Provider receipt, confirmed failure or uncertain outcome requiring reconciliation.
    gate: Timeout after a provider commit must not trigger a duplicate send/order/calendar entry.
    loop: Unknown effects go to station 11; reauthorization is required if the intended action changes.
    layers: 
      - L08
      - L09
    sprint: S2
    examples: 
      varun: Create the internal task and send the permitted notification. Store the provider receipt separately from task completion.
      ramya: Attach the reviewed notice to the assigned work; update a calendar only under the approved date and audience scope.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC01
        approach: Executor contributes bounded tool execution and integration/credential separation; SupaBiz owns business effect semantics.
      - project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 illustrates browser/environment handoff; persistent hosting is a separate service decision.
      - project: YC09
        approach: Agent Relay provides communication transport and job-scoped rooms; delivery does not prove business completion.
      - project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox contributes communication adapters, cancellation and distinct receipt/delivery stages.
      - project: YC13
        approach: herdr contributes node/job control patterns; terminal injection is not the restaurant transaction interface.
  - id: 11
    name: Verify, reconcile & close
    phase: PROVE & IMPROVE
    question: Did the intended result happen?
    purpose: Check real outcomes and missing effects before reporting success. Maintain the difference between delivered, acknowledged, completed and verified.
    parts: 
      - id: 11.1
        name: Outcome observer
        deliverable: Read back provider state or collect domain-specific completion evidence.
        mode: Build
      - id: 11.2
        name: Reconciliation queue
        deliverable: Resolve unknown outcomes, missing receipts and contradictions.
        mode: Build
      - id: 11.3
        name: Business closure rules
        deliverable: Define valid proof and who can accept the completed work.
        mode: Build
      - id: 11.4
        name: Audit & projections
        deliverable: Append result history and refresh scoped dashboards/search.
        mode: Build
      - id: 11.5
        name: Owner feedback
        deliverable: Show outcome, evidence, remaining blockers and meaningful summaries.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Attempt ledger, provider receipts, worker updates and new evidence.
    outputs: Verified completion, confirmed failure, partial completion or unresolved outcome.
    gate: A successful tool response cannot close a real-world task without its required evidence.
    loop: Failures retry only after reconciliation; changed facts return to station 07 and unresolved work to station 08.
    layers: 
      - L05
      - L07
      - L08
      - L01
    sprint: S2
    examples: 
      varun: A follow-up photo and manager check close the visible leak task. Invoice discrepancies remain exceptions for the CA.
      ramya: Acknowledged assignment is distinct from a filed document; proof of filing is required for that task’s closure.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC07
        approach: Sidekick contributes verified operational closure rather than stopping at report creation.
      - project: YC08
        approach: Marble contributes receiving/invoice/credit reconciliation before settlement.
      - project: YC18
        approach: Definite contributes evidence-based checks and useful unresolved states.
      - project: YC14
        approach: Terse distinguishes committed internal state from independently verified external effects.
      - project: YC09
        approach: Agent Relay highlights the distinction between communication receipts and actual work outcomes.
      - project: YC05
        approach: Praxis contributes work readiness, ownership and completion in the context of a matter.
  - id: 12
    name: Learn, evaluate & release
    phase: PROVE & IMPROVE
    question: Will the next case be better?
    purpose: Turn reviewed corrections and real incidents into scoped improvements. Evaluate off the live path; release only changes that pass protected quality and cost gates.
    parts: 
      - id: 12.1
        name: Correction capture
        deliverable: Preserve original evidence, old/new values and reason.
        mode: Build
      - id: 12.2
        name: Scoped proposal
        deliverable: Separate one-off fixes from reusable mapping, memory or procedure changes.
        mode: Build
      - id: 12.3
        name: Regression & held-out worlds
        deliverable: Versioned stateful cases, forbidden effects and protected answers.
        mode: Build
      - id: 12.4
        name: Release comparison
        deliverable: Quality, coverage, human effort, latency and full workflow cost.
        mode: Build
      - id: 12.5
        name: Versioned rollout
        deliverable: Review, activate, canary, observe and roll back a change.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Reviewed corrections, failures, incident traces and measured outcomes.
    outputs: Approved new workflow/context version or a rejected improvement proposal.
    gate: No customer’s correction becomes a global rule by default; a lower-cost change must preserve required outcome quality.
    loop: Reviewed changes return to stations 03/04; new events continue through station 05.
    layers: 
      - L10
      - L06
      - L05
    sprint: S0–S2, expanded S5
    examples: 
      varun: A corrected supplier alias becomes a Consu-scoped mapping only after tests; it does not silently affect ForeFathers.
      ramya: A matter matching error becomes a regression case across courts and similar case numbers, not an unchecked memory note.
    comparisons: 
      - project: YC04
        approach: Asakana’s correction-driven UX is the priority inspiration; the underlying training mechanism is not established by demos.
      - project: YC06
        approach: Hue turns production incidents into repeatable cases and release comparisons.
      - project: YC17
        approach: Rystic contributes stateful simulated services, fault injection and outcome/forbidden-effect grading.
      - project: YC12
        approach: GrepAI contributes procedure optimization with draft/tested/active boundaries.
      - project: YC15
        approach: Shire inspires categorized reviewed observation corrections; evaluation must include coverage and false alerts.
      - project: YC18
        approach: Definite supports measured model substitution; no model is trusted solely by brand or fluency.
foundations: 
  - id: F1
    name: Security & data lifecycle
    purpose: Enforced at every station, including files, exports, derived context and logs.
    parts: 
      - id: F1.1
        name: Tenant isolation & policy enforcement
        mode: Build
        deliverable: Runtime-role tests and audience-scoped data access.
      - id: F1.2
        name: Secrets & cryptographic primitives
        mode: Reuse
        deliverable: Maintained secrets/encryption services with scoped access.
      - id: F1.3
        name: Retention, deletion & export
        mode: Build
        deliverable: Artifact-specific lifecycle and invalidation, not just a UI delete.
      - id: F1.4
        name: Audit & incident response
        mode: Build
        deliverable: Protected decision/effect history and an operational response plan.
    projects: 
      - YC01

roadmap: 
  - id: S0
    name: Baseline, contracts and one test world
    estimate: 1 week
    depends: 

    owner: Platform lead + product owner
    deliver: 
      - Locate and audit actual SupaBiz product code; reproduce the dossier’s fresh-intake failure.
      - Pin source, record, grant, decision, action and evaluation contracts. Inventory actual implementation versus reported behavior.
      - Create synthetic Consu/ForeFathers/Arkaj identities and a small stateful world; establish case manifest, clock and protected scorer.
    gate: Every observed failure has a source/run/evidence ID and responsible layer. Wrong-tenant, duplicate and wrong-record controls demonstrably fail the test oracle.
    not_yet: No framework migration, procurement or claim that prior 24/24 known cases represent general accuracy.
  - id: S1
    name: Reliable capture and protected evidence
    estimate: 2 weeks
    depends: 
      - S0
    owner: Integration engineer + platform lead
    deliver: 
      - Selected WhatsApp group and Gmail intake with durable journal/cursors, replay, gaps and edit/delete handling.
      - Authentication, business/matter grants, credential broker, runtime-role DB isolation and object access.
      - PDF/image/voice pipeline with bounded workers, provenance and missing-evidence states.
    gate: Crash/reconnect/expired-cursor tests preserve events; seeded cross-scope reads fail; source lag and missing coverage visible. Originals and derivatives recover coherently.
    not_yet: No autonomous external writes; no blanket desktop or microphone capture.
  - id: S2
    name: One complete photo-to-task workflow
    estimate: 2–3 weeks
    depends: 
      - S1
    owner: Product engineer + platform lead + restaurant manager
    deliver: 
      - Staff capture receipt, evidence drawer, manager correction, assignment, acknowledgement, reminders and verified closure.
      - Typed action gateway, approval binding, uncertain-send reconciliation and current-permission recheck.
      - Temporal-versus-existing-worker recovery spike; select one owner before live multi-day work.
      - Very important correction loop v1: one-off versus scoped rule, reviewed promotion and regression case.
    gate: A new unseen photo flows to a correct verified outcome through restart, correction and cancellation. No duplicate effects or unauthorized disclosures in the critical suite. Pilot starts read-only/shadow, then limited authorized actions.
    not_yet: No full ERP, generic agent marketplace, automated accounting or native messenger.
  - id: S3
    name: Receiving, invoices and accountant handoff
    estimate: 2 weeks
    depends: 
      - S2
    owner: Domain/integration engineer + manager/CA
    deliver: 
      - Distinct order, receipt, stocktake, movement, invoice and credit records; explicit units and source authority.
      - Opening-count/cutover procedure before reliable balances; split/partial receiving and duplicate allocations.
      - Reviewed reconciliation packet for existing accountant system; exports and remote posting are distinct.
    gate: Golden cases retain correct balances under late movements, returns, duplicate photos and corrections. Quantity/price mismatches stay visible; no unsupported GST/accounting treatment or automatic payment.
    not_yet: No demand-forecast optimization, supplier auto-pay or POS replacement.
  - id: S4
    name: Ramya’s existing-matter workflow in shadow mode
    estimate: 2 weeks; can overlap S3 only with a separate staffed lane
    depends: 
      - S2
    owner: Product/integration engineer + Ramya + responsible lawyer
    deliver: 
      - Reviewed matter directory and compound identity; notice/hearing/work deadline types and source locators.
      - Evidence-backed change packet, assignee acceptance, document readiness and controlled calendar projection.
      - Superseded notices invalidate stale decisions/reminders; matter grants propagate to files and replies.
    gate: Held-out notices match correct matters or abstain usefully; no unreviewed schedule-critical writes. Domain reviewer validates dates; revoked assignees cannot receive documents.
    not_yet: No legal advice, inferred filing deadlines, automatic new-matter creation or automatic client updates.
  - id: S5
    name: Pilot economics, hardening and measured optimization
    estimate: 2 weeks per released pilot; extends if gates fail
    depends: 
      - S2
    owner: Platform lead + QA + pilot owner
    deliver: 
      - Only evaluate workflows whose own gates passed; S3/S4 are prerequisites for inventory/legal release respectively.
      - Coherent restore, retention/deletion lineage, permission revocation, provider outages, quotas and unknown outcomes.
      - Compare model/provider and governed-procedure candidates; costs include media, review/support and idle infrastructure.
      - Add one API-less browser or short-video case only if it materially unblocks the pilot.
    gate: Pre-agreed quality/review/cost thresholds pass on held-out and observed pilot work, with sample sizes and failure categories. Rollback and support runbooks exercised. No measured benefit is claimed before this evidence.
    not_yet: No expanding scope to hide poor first-workflow completion.
  - id: S6
    name: Demand-led collaboration and device expansion
    estimate: Later; separately scoped
    depends: 
      - S5
    owner: Product + platform
    deliver: 
      - Object-linked app chat and partner job rooms with scoped invitations and revocation.
      - Optional Agent Relay transport, limited desktop capture or Shire-style camera events after purpose/rights/cost validation.
      - Evaluate Terse or dedicated tenant environments only for a measured scaling requirement; expand connector/domain packs independently.
    gate: The added capability improves an existing workflow at acceptable total cost and passes the same authority/evidence/outcome controls.
    not_yet: No automatic agent federation or mandatory migration from WhatsApp.
